newsitem.title: USA: Iridium says Monday launch delayed after explosion.
newsitem.headline: Iridium says Monday launch delayed after explosion.

text.p: Iridium LLC said Friday its planned launch of three satellites Monday would be delayed because of the explosion of a Delta II rocket in Florida.
The rocket that exploded earlier Friday is the same type that was to launch the Iridium satellites.
"No question about it. It certainly will do so," Iridium spokesman John Windolph said when asked if the explosion would delay the launch.

A spokeswoman for McDonnell Douglas Corp, whose Delta II rocket exploded Friday just after blastoff from Cape Canaveral Air Station in Florida, said industry practice was not to launch another rocket of the same type until an investigation into the cause of an explosion was completed.

In a telephone interview, the spokeswoman could not say how long the investigation would take. The investigation was being conducted by the U.S. Air Force, which had a $40 million navigational satellite on the rocket, she said.

The Iridium satellite launch had already been postponed on January 8 and January 9, the second time when a problem was discovered with the thermal protection on the Delta II rocket, the Iridium consortium said.
Motorola Inc has about a 25 percent stake in the consortium, which is working to provide a global telecommunications network using 66 low-orbit satellites.
The launch delay should not impact activation of the system, Windolph said.
"We don't expect any impact on our commercial activation schedule, which is slated for September '98," he said in a telephone interview.

The satellites could be moved to a Russian Khrunishev Space Research and Production Center Enterprise Proton rocket or a China Great Wall Industry Corp Long March II C-SD rocket, but such a move would delay the launch by about 50 days, Windolph said.
The Iridium consortium comprises 17 companies including Motorola, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co Ltd of Taiwan and Raytheon Co.
